_WHAT_THIS_FILE_IS: STAGING ONLY. Candidate rows for data/regions.json, surfaced 16 Nov 2026 by web search while widening the validation set beyond the psychiatric proteins (the outstanding task named in CLAUDE.md). NOTHING HERE IS VERIFIED. Every entry is SNIPPET grade: search-engine summary of an abstract, never a publisher PDF anyone opened. No row moves into regions.json until someone reads the paper and sets verified_against_publisher_pdf. Keeping them here rather than in regions.json is deliberate: regions.json is the asset intended for publication with its own DOI, and must not carry unread rows.
_SCHEMA_CHANGE_16_NOV_2026: KEEP CIRCULAR ROWS, LABELLED -- author decision, applied to regions.json and mirrored here. The two lists candidates_CLEAN and candidates_CIRCULAR_DO_NOT_ADD are merged into ONE list whose members each carry circularity_status. Nothing is deleted. A candidate found to be circular is still a candidate: it enters the published set labelled, is excluded from the primary statistic, and is reported as its own stratum. See _SCHEMA_CIRCULARITY in data/regions.json for the governing definitions. SECOND SCHEMA POINT, same day: a THIRD provenance grade now exists between SNIPPET and READ -- 'READ BY AUDIT SUBAGENT'. It is strictly weaker than READ. It is recorded because three audits returned verbatim quotes that are worth keeping, and strictly weaker because an agent that reads a paper and an author who reads a paper are not the same witness.

_THE_PREMISE_AUDIT_THAT_CAME_FIRST.question: CLAUDE.md says to widen to 'every protein with fragment-level aggregation mapping'. Before listing candidates: what actually qualifies?
_THE_PREMISE_AUDIT_THAT_CAME_FIRST.finding: THE CLEAN CLASS IS MUCH NARROWER THAN THE LITERATURE LOOKS, AND THE SEARCH SURFACE IS DOMINATED BY PREDICTION-GUIDED REGIONS. Of eight candidate regions surfaced in the first sweep, THREE were found by an aggregation predictor and then validated experimentally. Those are circular for a predictor benchmark no matter how good the experiments are -- scoring a predictor against a region that predictor's ancestors chose is not a test. This is the found_by column doing its job at the survey stage rather than after the compute.
_THE_PREMISE_AUDIT_THAT_CAME_FIRST.operational_criterion: A row qualifies as CLEAN only if the region was localised by truncation, deletion, substitution or an unbiased screen, WITH NO PREDICTOR IN THE DISCOVERY PATH. Prediction used AFTER mapping, as a post-hoc mechanistic check, does not contaminate the row -- that is the DISC1 384-415 situation, re-checked 16 Nov 2026 and still clean.
_THE_PREMISE_AUDIT_THAT_CAME_FIRST.consequence_for_the_floor: The floor of 15 rows may be reachable, but not from a casual sweep. Expect to discard roughly a third of what the literature offers. If the clean class turns out to be too small, THAT IS THE FINDING and must be reported, not worked around -- CLAUDE.md rule 3.
_THE_PREMISE_AUDIT_THAT_CAME_FIRST.UPDATE_16_NOV_2026_AFTER_READING_ONE_PAP: READING FLIPPED THE BEST LEAD FROM CLEAN TO CIRCULAR. At SNIPPET level the apoA-I series looked like the cleanest candidate in the sweep: 'using a series of deletion variants' reads as unbiased mapping. The full text shows all four variants were designed to delete segments that AmylPred2 and Zyggregator had ranked, with the prediction tracks plotted in Figure 1B. CONTAMINATION RATE: 3 of 10 at snippet level, 6 of 10 after reading ONE of the ten. IMPLICATION FOR THE WHOLE SWEEP: snippet-level found_by assessment is not merely unverified, it is BIASED TOWARDS FALSE CLEAN, because abstracts describe the assay and bury the construct design. No candidate may be counted toward the floor of 15 on snippet evidence. AND A STRUCTURAL WARNING ABOUT THE FIELD: when a predicted segment gets deleted and the deletion works, that is published as experimental mapping. The literature therefore contains many 'experimentally mapped' regions whose boundaries came from a predictor. DISC1 384-415 and TRIOBP-1 324-348 are unusual precisely because truncation came first and prediction after.

candidates.why_excluded: [field name retained for history; this row is NO LONGER EXCLUDED, it is KEPT AND LABELLED] FOUND BY PREDICTION. THE WHOLE SERIES WAS DESIGNED TO DELETE PREDICTED SEGMENTS. Verdict reversed on reading the paper; the abstract concealed it.
the_quotes_that_decide_it: Introduction, p.13515: 'Sequence-based analyses of N-terminal residues 1-100 in apoA-I PREDICT that there are two major aggregation-prone segments (residues 14-22 and 50-58) together with a minor segment (residues 69-72) in which the rank order of aggregation propensity is residues 14-22 > residues 50-58 > residues 69-72.'

Results, p.13516: 'The deletion variants, delta-14-22, delta-50-58, and delta-68-76, lack the highly amyloidogenic segments of residues 14-22, 50-58, and 69-72, respectively (10), whereas the delta-32-40 variant lacks the PUTATIVE LOOP REGION between two beta-strands from residues 14-31 to 41-58 (23).'

Figure 1B caption: 'Amyloid propensity prediction was generated using the consensus algorithm AMYLPRED2 (54). beta-Aggregation propensity was calculated with the ZYGGREGATOR method (55).' Figure 1B plots both tracks with 14-22, 32-40, 50-58 and 68-76 drawn on it.
candidates.why_this_is_the_worst_case_of_circularit: AMYLPRED2 IS IN THIS PROJECT'S OWN LEGACY PREDICTOR SET. Scoring AmylPred2 against a region AmylPred2 selected is not a test of anything. Zyggregator (Tartaglia 2008) is an aggregation predictor too. Even delta-32-40, the apparent 'loop' control, was chosen from a predicted beta-strand topology (ref 23, a FRET-based model).
candidates.is_anything_in_the_paper_still_usable: NO CLEAN ROW. The pyrene excimer mapping (Fig 6) IS a real experimental measurement of which segments sit in the amyloid core -- positions 22 and 52 give high excimer ratios, positions 2, 8, 36, 72 and 81 low -- but THE LABELLING POSITIONS WERE THEMSELVES CHOSEN FROM THE PREDICTED SEGMENTS. It measures proximity at pre-selected sites; it does not map the core de novo. Experimental readout, prediction-guided sampling.
candidates.the_one_legitimate_use_and_its_limit: CIRCULARITY IS TOOL-SPECIFIC. The region was chosen by AmylPred2 and Zyggregator, not by AggreProt (2024), AggrescanAI (2026) or any PLM. So apoA-I 14-22 could serve as a POSITIVE CONTROL for the modern arm only -- a region where experiment confirms that prediction was right. BUT IT CANNOT TEST THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS: a region selected because legacy tools ranked it top is, by construction, a predictable region. Scoring modern tools on it measures whether modern agrees with legacy, not whether modern recovers what experiment found and legacy missed. Use it as a labelled positive control with that bias stated, or not at all.
candidates.what_the_paper_does_establish_well: READ IN FULL, and it is good work. 14-22 is NECESSARY: no ThT increase, no random-coil to beta transition by CD, no fibrils by AFM or TEM, only small spherical aggregates, and reduced cytotoxicity in HEK293. 32-40 and 50-58 are NOT necessary but slow nucleation and growth. 50-58 entropically drives nucleation (delta-S* for nucleation flips from +55 to -281 J/mol/K). 68-76 INHIBITS fibril growth enthalpically. Construct throughout: apoA-I 1-83/G26R, a disease-variant N-terminal fragment expressed in E. coli as a thioredoxin fusion leaving two extra residues (Gly-Ser) at the N terminus -- not full-length wild type.

candidates.circularity_basis: CLEAN -- but NOT for the reason the audit subagent gave, and the correction matters. THE AGENT REPORTED "no algorithm named anywhere in the paper". THAT IS FALSE: predicted beta-structure is mentioned at least five times, including in the Abstract ("This motif coincides with the highest predicted beta-structure potential in tau"), in the Results heading ("...Represents a Minimal Interaction Motif with a Predicted beta Conformation") and in the Discussion ("are the only two spots in the tau sequence where a beta conformation is strongly predicted"). THE ROW IS STILL CLEAN BECAUSE EVERY ONE OF THOSE IS POST HOC -- prediction is used to EXPLAIN the scan result, never to select the peptides -- which is the permitted direction under the operational criterion. But the distinction is "prediction appears, in the allowed direction", not "prediction is absent", and a reviewer will find those sentences in ten seconds. State it ourselves.

candidates.TENTH_INCONSISTENCY_SCAN_SCOPE: THE PAPER CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON WHAT WAS SCANNED. The Abstract says the motif came from "overlapping peptides derived from the FULL tau sequence". Figure 4 says "The region of tau from L253 in repeat 1 to D348 in repeat 4" -- 96 residues, not the 441-residue protein. THESE ARE NOT THE SAME CLAIM, and the difference decides what the row means: an unbiased scan of a PROTEIN, or an unbiased scan of a PRE-SELECTED DOMAIN. Figure 4 is almost certainly right and the Abstract is loose. The row is still clean either way, because the domain boundary came from GluC proteolysis rather than from a predictor -- but DO NOT DESCRIBE THIS AS A WHOLE-PROTEIN SCAN. The audit subagent gave L253-D348 and was right about the range while being wrong about the algorithms.

candidates.circularity_basis: DOWNGRADED 16 Nov 2026 ON READING FIGURES 1 AND 4, AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN A JUDGEMENT CALL. PHF6* lies at 275-280, i.e. in the FIRST SIX RESIDUES OF R2. The probe used in the peptide scan is PHF43 = [N265-E338 dR2] -- R2 IS DELETED FROM THE PROBE. So this experiment could not, and did not, establish PHF6* the way it established PHF6. The paper treats it accordingly: the Abstract names ONE motif, "a minimal hexapeptide interaction motif of 306VQIVYK311", and Figure 4 calls PHF6* "the ANALOGOUS sequence in R2". PHF6* IS THEREFORE IDENTIFIED BY SEQUENCE ANALOGY TO PHF6, NOT BY ITS OWN SIGNAL. That is not predictor-circular -- analogy to an experimentally mapped motif is not an algorithm -- but it is a HOMOLOGY INFERENCE, and it must not be entered as a second independent clean row. Entering it as one would have double-counted a single experimental result. TO RESCUE IT: von Bergen 2001 (J Biol Chem 276:48165) is the FTDP-17 paper where DeltaK280, which sits inside PHF6*, is characterised; that is where independent evidence would live.

candidates.evidence: NECESSARY AND SUFFICIENT for fibrillization, by four independent lines stated in the abstract: (1) human beta-synuclein is highly homologous but LACKS THESE 12 RESIDUES and does not assemble -- a NATURAL NEGATIVE; (2) introducing a single charged residue slows polymerization and a deletion abrogates assembly; (3) the stretch is PROTEASE-RESISTANT in filaments, i.e. it forms the core; (4) synthetic 12-mers self-polymerize AND seed full-length alpha-synuclein.
candidates.construct: Multiple: full-length human alpha-synuclein with substitutions and an internal deletion; human beta-synuclein as the natural comparator; isolated synthetic 12-mer peptide. Sufficiency is shown in the PEPTIDE, necessity in the FULL-LENGTH protein -- both, which is rare among the rows in this file.
candidates.found_by: COMPARATIVE SEQUENCE ALIGNMENT AGAINST A PARALOGUE. NO PREDICTOR, NO PROPENSITY ANALYSIS OF ANY KIND -- the full text settles the question the abstract left open. Results: "Alignment of the primary sequences of human a- and b-syn showed two major regional differences between the proteins. A stretch of hydrophobic amino acids in the middle of a-syn is absent in b-syn (Fig. 1)." Discussion: "We sought to explain the dramatic difference in assembly properties of human a- and b-syn by comparing their sequences." The 71/82 boundaries come from that alignment and from nothing else. Dated 2001, before TANGO, AGGRESCAN, FoldAmyloid or ZipperDB existed.
candidates.source: Giasson BI, Murray IV, Trojanowski JQ, Lee VM (2001) J Biol Chem 276(4):2380-6, doi:10.1074/jbc.M008919200, PMID 11060312
candidates.provenance: READ IN FULL, 16 Nov 2026, publisher PDF supplied by the author. Supersedes the abstract-grade entry made earlier the same day; four things changed on reading.
candidates.circularity_basis: CLEAN, and it REVERSES the audit's fear that the alpha-synuclein branch might yield nothing. The discovery path is a natural deletion in a paralogue plus protease resistance -- no algorithm, and no algorithm of the relevant kind existed in 2001. This is the same experimental logic as the natural-negative argument in inventory row C1 (C. elegans TDP-1) and it is strong.
candidates.sequence_provenance: VERIFIED AGAINST UniProt P37840 (140 aa) BY THE MAIN SESSION, 16 Nov 2026. The abstract prints "(71)VTGVTAVAQKTV(82)"; UniProt residues 71-82 are VTGVTAVAQKTV. EXACT MATCH. The paper's own numbering is therefore correct -- no ninth slip here.
TWO_CAVEATS_THAT_LIMIT_WHAT_IT_CAN_TEST: IT IS A REGION THE PREDICTORS DO FIND. 71-82 overlaps NACore 68-78 by eight residues, and NACore was later selected by ZipperDB (see the NACore row above). So this row is CLEAN BY FOUND_BY but is not a test of the central hypothesis: it cannot show that predictors miss experimentally mapped regions, because this is a region they hit. Its correct role is a LABELLED TRUE-POSITIVE / POSITIVE CONTROL -- valuable for the dataset, neutral for the headline.

IT DOES NOT SUPPORT THE GATEKEEPER INVERSION. Computed by the main session from the verified sequence: 71-82 is 8.3% proline-plus-charge (one lysine, K80), BELOW the worst deposited zipper in scripts/gatekeeper_density.py (16.7%). It is a conventional hydrophobic zipper. The inversion therefore stands at n=1 (TRIOBP-1 324-348, 48.0%) against THREE regions that behave as the field's rules predict: DISC1 384-415 at 18.8%, alpha-syn 71-82 at 8.3%, and the NAC domain 61-95 at 8.6%. Each clean row added so far has made the inversion lonelier, not better supported. That is the honest trend and it should be reported as such.
candidates.the_one_thing_the_full_text_must_still_s: Whether any sequence-based propensity analysis was used to NARROW within the hydrophobic NAC domain beyond the beta-synuclein alignment. The phrase "the middle of the hydrophobic domain" is almost certainly not contamination -- the NAC domain was defined experimentally from Alzheimer plaque material in 1993, not predicted -- but the precise 71/82 boundaries should be traced in the Results before this row is promoted.
candidates.CORRECTION_TO_THE_ABSTRACT_GRADE_ENTRY: I WROTE THAT PROTEOLYSIS CORROBORATED THE 71-82 BOUNDARY. IT DOES NOT, AND THAT WAS AN OVERSTATEMENT. The protease-resistant fragments F1-F3 map to the NAC region: "These fragments mapped to the middle hydrophobic region and contained amino acids 61-95." All three merely CONTAIN 71-82. So proteolysis localises the core to 61-95 at 35-residue resolution and is CORROBORATING AT LOWER RESOLUTION; the 12-residue boundary rests on the beta-synuclein alignment alone. The row is still CLEAN -- the discovery path is not a predictor either way -- but it rests on ONE line of evidence for its boundaries, not two.
candidates.NINTH_SLIP_AND_THE_FIRST_THAT_IS_A_SEQUE: THE METHODS PRINT THE SYNTHETIC PEPTIDE AS "VTGVTAVAQKTA", ENDING IN ALANINE. The title, abstract, Results, Discussion and UniProt P37840 all give 71-82 as VTGVTAVAQKTV, ending in VALINE. Verified: P37840 position 82 is Val. SO THE METHODS STRING IS WRONG AT THE LAST RESIDUE. Why it matters more than the eight numbering slips already tallied: this is the described sequence of THE PEPTIDE THAT CARRIES THE ENTIRE SUFFICIENCY CLAIM -- Figs 4E (self-assembly), 4F (co-assembly) and 7A/7B (light scattering, seeding). Almost certainly a typo, because every other mention is correct, BUT IT CANNOT BE PROVED FROM THE PAPER, and if the peptide really was V82A then sufficiency was shown for a sequence one residue off the claimed region. Record as a typo; do not silently assume it.

what_the_full_text_adds.construct_exact: All synuclein cDNAs subcloned into NdeI/HindIII of pRK172, expressed in E. coli BL21(DE3); assembly in 100 mM sodium acetate pH 7.0 at 37 C with continuous shaking; sedimentation 100,000 x g, 20 min.
what_the_full_text_adds.necessity: D71-82 did not assemble by sedimentation OR by EM even after SIX WEEKS, and showed no random-coil-to-beta transition by CD. It also neither inhibited nor co-assembled with wild-type a-syn.
what_the_full_text_adds.sufficiency: Synthetic 71-82 self-assembles into filaments (11.3 +/- 2.8 nm) and promotes assembly of full-length a-syn. Filaments from the peptide alone are STRAIGHTER than full-length filaments -- a morphological difference the paper notes and does not explain.
what_the_full_text_adds.the_carboxy_terminal_control: The a/b-syn hybrid (a-syn 1-97 + b-syn 87-134) assembles at the SAME rate as wild type. So the divergent C-terminus is NOT responsible for b-syn's failure to assemble. A real negative control, and it isolates the 12-mer.

candidates.THIS_DIRECTLY_TESTS_THE_GATEKEEPER_PREMI: A76R AND A76E PUT A SINGLE CHARGED RESIDUE INTO THE MIDDLE OF A HYDROPHOBIC AGGREGATION CORE, AND NEITHER ABOLISHED ASSEMBLY. A76R was mostly assembled by 4 days; A76E was slower but by 9 days "polymerized into fibrils that were morphologically indistinguishable from those generated from the wild-type protein." The paper states the conclusion outright: "these results demonstrate that the introduction of a single charged residue IS NOT SUFFICIENT to disrupt the hydrophobic intermolecular interactions driving filament formation." WHY THIS MATTERS TO THIS PROJECT: the gatekeeper hypothesis treats proline and charge as aggregation SUPPRESSORS. Here, in a clean system, one charge DELAYS and does not prevent. That does NOT refute the density claim -- one charge is not 48% density, and the dose-response could still be steep higher up -- but it is a measured caution against treating gatekeeper residues as switches, it is from 2001, and it should be CITED rather than discovered again.

_THE_PRIOR_ART_FINDING_THAT_MATTERS_MORE.finding: MURRAY ET AL. 2017 (Cell 171:615, FUS) ALREADY PUBLISHES BOTH HALVES OF THIS PROJECT'S SHAPE, FOR A DIFFERENT PROTEIN.
_THE_PRIOR_ART_FINDING_THAT_MATTERS_MORE.quote_predictors: Discussion, 'What determines the fibril core?': 'Aggrescan, FISH, FoldAmyloid, MetAmyl, and PASTA 2.0 predict a low propensity for amyloid formation across the FUS-LC'; ZipperDB, Zyggregator and WALTZ 'predict that certain short segments of FUS-LC may form amyloidlike structures' but 'with no consensus on the identities of these segments'. _THE_PRIOR_ART_FINDING_THAT_MATTERS_MORE.quote_composition: Same section: 'The amino acid composition of residues 39-95 (21.1% Gly, 31.6% Ser, 17.5% Gln, 14.0% Tyr, and 10.5% Thr)' is 'not very different from that of residues 1-214', and 'also not very different from that of residues 96-165'.
what_it_does_NOT_pre_empt: The PLM novelty claim, PREREGISTRATION 5.2. Murray 2017 is a 2017 paper on FUS; it runs no PLM-era tool and touches neither DISC1 nor TRIOBP-1. That claim is INTACT.

The legacy-failure premise, which CLAUDE.md already declares cited evidence rather than a result to establish. Murray 2017 is a THIRD independent instance and therefore STRENGTHENS the premise rather than damaging it.

The specific gatekeeper INVERSION. Murray's claim is that composition fails to DISCRIMINATE the core. This project's claim is stronger and directionally different: TRIOBP-1 324-348 is 48.0% proline-plus-charge, i.e. composed of the residues the field deliberately engineers IN to SUPPRESS aggregation, and was mapped as aggregation-critical anyway. 'Composition is uninformative' and 'composition points the wrong way' are not the same claim.
_THE_PRIOR_ART_FINDING_THAT_MATTERS_MORE.what_it_DOES_pre_empt: The generic compositional move. This project cannot present 'and composition does not explain why the predictors missed it' as a new insight -- that is in print, in Cell, with numbers, since 2017. Only the inversion is left, and by this project's OWN accounting the inversion is n=1: scripts/gatekeeper_density.py prints THE SEPARATION DOES NOT GENERALISE, because DISC1 384-415 came in at 18.8%, just 2.1 points above the worst deposited zipper. So the surviving novel claim rests on a single region.
_THE_PRIOR_ART_FINDING_THAT_MATTERS_MORE.action_required_before_freeze: The author must decide whether an n=1 inversion, with the generic version pre-empted, is a headline or a discussion paragraph. This is a framing decision, not a data problem, and it belongs to the author, not to Claude.

_ALPHA_SYNUCLEIN_BRANCH_RESOLVED_16_NOV_: THE BRANCH IS NOT EMPTY. The audit assessed 6 alpha-synuclein regions and found 5 CIRCULAR, leaving 71-82 UNDECIDABLE behind Cloudflare and warning that alpha-synuclein might contribute no clean row at all. The full structured abstract, read directly, settles it: 71-82 is CLEAN, by comparative homology plus limited proteolysis, in 2001, before any predictor under test existed. It is also the only row in this file shown NECESSARY AND SUFFICIENT with sufficiency demonstrated in an isolated synthetic peptide. BUT read its two caveats: it is a region the predictors DO find, and at 8.3% gatekeeper density it makes the inversion claim lonelier.
_THE_PATTERN_ACROSS_THE_CLEAN_ROWS_AND_W: THREE CLEAN ROWS IN A ROW TURN OUT TO BE REGIONS THE PREDICTORS FIND: alpha-syn 71-82 (overlaps ZipperDB-selected NACore by 8 residues), tau PHF6 306-311 and tau PHF6* 275-280 ("the only two spots in the tau sequence where a beta conformation is strongly predicted"). THIS IS NOT A COINCIDENCE AND IT IS A PROPERTY OF THE FIELD, NOT OF OUR SWEEP. A region gets mapped cleanly and early when it is a classic short hydrophobic or beta-prone motif -- which is precisely what the predictors were built to detect. The regions predictors MISS are rare in the literature for the same reason they are interesting: they are unusual. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE BENCHMARK, AND IT IS A RULE 2 PROBLEM, NOT A SOURCING PROBLEM. Widening the validation set mostly adds TRUE POSITIVES. True positives cannot discriminate modern from legacy predictors, because both classes hit them. The rows that discriminate are the handful where experiment and prediction DISAGREE -- currently TRIOBP-1 324-348 and DISC1 384-415, i.e. the two we started with.
